title: The Finding of Moses
creator: Jacopo Tintoretto (Jacopo Robusti)
description: A Venetian interpretation of the rescue of the infant Moses. The figures and landscape offer a different visual treatment from nineteenth-century Bible illustrations.
caution: The date is uncertain. Dress and landscape belong to the artist’s interpretation, not an archaeological reconstruction of Egypt.

passages.note: Pharaoh’s daughter finds Moses, and his mother becomes his nurse.

source.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
source.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Gwynne Andrews Fund, 1939.

alt: The infant Moses being received by women beside a river, painted by Tintoretto

title: Hagar in the Wilderness
creator: Camille Corot
description: Hagar and Ishmael appear in a wide, arid landscape beneath a distant angel. The scale of the setting emphasizes their isolation.
caution: The museum notes that the landscape draws partly on studies in France. This is biblical narrative painting, not a photograph of Beersheba.

passages.note: An interpretation of Hagar and Ishmael in the wilderness and the promise of help.

source.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
source.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Rogers Fund, 1938.

alt: Hagar and Ishmael in a broad rocky landscape with an angel above, painted by Corot

title: Moses Striking the Rock
creator: Abraham Bloemaert
description: A crowded scene of people and vessels around the gift of water. Moses appears farther back rather than dominating the foreground.
caution: Includes artistic nudity and later allegorical imagery. The composition is an interpretation of water in the wilderness, not a reconstruction of the event.

passages.note: An editorial connection to the account of water from the rock; the painting adds figures and symbolism.

source.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
source.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Purchase, Gift of Mary V. T. Eberstadt, by exchange, 1972.

alt: People carrying vessels around water in the wilderness, painted by Abraham Bloemaert

title: Moses
creator: Lorenzo Monaco (Piero di Giovanni)
description: A gold-ground panel presents Moses holding two tablets. The luminous surface offers a different visual language from naturalistic narrative painting.
caution: The tablets contain pseudo-Hebrew lettering, not a reliable transcription of the Ten Commandments. This is a later symbolic portrait.

passages.note: A symbolic portrait accompanying the Ten Commandments; not a depiction of the exact moment of their delivery.
Moses and the tablets as a later artistic interpretation alongside the commandments.

source.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
source.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Gwynne Andrews Fund, and Bequest of Mabel Choate, in memory of her father, Joseph Hodges Choate, by exchange, 1965.

alt: Moses holding tablets against a gold background, painted by Lorenzo Monaco

title: The Annunciation
creator: Botticelli (Alessandro di Mariano Filipepi)
description: Gabriel and Mary face one another across an architectural interior. Receding columns and floor lines give the small panel a sense of depth.
caution: The architecture is an imagined Renaissance interior, not evidence for the appearance of Mary’s home.

passages.note: An interpretation of Gabriel’s announcement to Mary.

source.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
source.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Robert Lehman Collection, 1975.

alt: Gabriel approaching Mary through a columned room in Botticelli’s Annunciation

title: The Denial of Saint Peter
creator: Caravaggio (Michelangelo Merisi)
description: A few illuminated faces and gestures emerge from a dark setting. The concentrated composition gives Peter’s denial a strikingly intimate treatment.
caution: The figures and lighting are artistic interpretation; the painting is not an eyewitness image of the courtyard.

passages.note: Peter is accused of following Jesus and denies knowing him.
An artistic interpretation of Peter’s denial.

title: Christ Carrying the Cross
creator: El Greco (Domenikos Theotokopoulos)
description: Christ embraces the cross and looks upward. The museum describes a devotional image rather than a complete narrative scene.
caution: A devotional interpretation without a recognizable setting. Do not treat it as a reconstruction of the route to the crucifixion.

passages.note: A devotional interpretation accompanying the reference to Jesus carrying the cross.

source.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
source.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Robert Lehman Collection, 1975.

alt: Christ holding the cross and looking upward, painted by El Greco

title: The Supper at Emmaus
creator: Velázquez (Diego Rodríguez de Silva y Velázquez)
description: Two disciples react to Christ at a table. Light, gesture and closely observed tableware draw attention to the moment of recognition.
caution: A seventeenth-century interpretation of the meal, not a reconstruction of the room or the disciples’ appearance.

passages.note: The disciples recognize Jesus in the breaking of bread.

source.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
source.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Bequest of Benjamin Altman, 1913.

alt: Christ and two disciples at a table in Velázquez’s Supper at Emmaus

title: The Adoration of the Magi
creator: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo
description: An animated oil sketch places the visitors and Holy Family among monumental architectural forms. Compare it with Giotto’s treatment of the same subject.
caution: The number, appearance and architectural setting of the visitors reflect later artistic tradition rather than details supplied by Matthew.

passages.note: A different artist’s interpretation of the visitors offering gifts.

source.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
source.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Rogers Fund, 1937.

alt: The Magi approaching the Holy Family beneath monumental ruins, painted by Tiepolo
